The son will most likely prevail, because he was the intended donee beneficiary of the contract (the owner promised to pay him, and the landscaper meant it as a graduation gift). The modification came after the landscaper had fully performed, and the son hadn't yet learned of the contract or relied on it. Under the Restatement (Second) §311 and the majority view, that late modification is still ineffective against a donee beneficiary, which points to B over C. The risk is that a court following the older rule, under which rights vest only on knowledge or reliance, would hold the modification effective.

CONFIDENCE: 62
